Preparing APSIM meteorological files with ag5Tools

ag5_apsim.Rmd

Overview

The APSIM crop modelling platform requires a site meteorological file containing daily weather observations with specific variable names, units, and header metadata. ag5_apsim() automates this workflow:

  1. Extracts the required AgERA5 variables from locally downloaded .nc files.
  2. Applies unit conversions (Kelvin → °C, J/m²/day → MJ/m²/day).
  3. Computes the site constants tav and amp.
  4. Writes a ready-to-use .met file (classic APSIM) or .csv + constants file (APSIM Next Generation).

Variable mapping

APSIM column AgERA5 variable Statistic Unit conversion
maxt Temperature-Air-2m Max-24h K → °C
mint Temperature-Air-2m Min-24h K → °C
rain Precipitation-Flux — none (mm/day)
radn Solar-Radiation-Flux — J/m²/day ÷ 1 000 000 → MJ/m²/day
wind Wind-Speed-10m Mean none (m/s)
vp Vapour-Pressure Mean none (hPa)
rh Relative-Humidity-2m — none (%)

maxt, mint, rain, and radn are the four variables required by APSIM for all simulations. wind, vp, and rh are optional but used by several crop modules.

Site constants: tav and amp

APSIM .met files carry two header constants derived from the weather record:

  • tav — annual average temperature (°C), computed as the mean of (maxt + mint) / 2 across all days.
  • amp — half the range between the warmest and coolest monthly mean temperatures (°C), computed as (max(monthly_mean_temp) - min(monthly_mean_temp)) / 2.

ag5_apsim() computes both constants automatically from the extracted data.

Controlling which variables are extracted

The variables argument accepts three forms:

Value Variables extracted
"all" (default) maxt, mint, rain, radn, wind, vp, rh
"required" maxt, mint, rain, radn
character vector any subset, e.g. c("maxt", "mint", "rain", "radn", "wind")

Examples

Return a data.frame (no file written)

When filename = NULL (the default), ag5_apsim() returns an annotated data.frame and prints the site constants to the console.

library(ag5Tools)

met <- ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),   # lon, lat — Arusha, Tanzania
  start_date = "2015-01-01",
  end_date   = "2015-12-31",
  variables  = "required",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data"
)

head(met)
#>   year day   maxt   mint  rain      radn
#> 1 2015   1  27.43  17.89  0.00  19.42
#> 2 2015   2  28.12  18.03  0.00  20.11
#> 3 2015   3  26.78  17.61  2.34  15.73
#> ...

attr(met, "tav")
attr(met, "amp")

Write a classic APSIM .met file

Set filename to a path without extension; ag5_apsim() appends .met.

ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2015-01-01",
  end_date   = "2015-12-31",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha_2015",
  format     = "classic"
)

The output file arusha_2015.met looks like:

! Generated by ag5Tools
latitude = -3.37 (degrees)
longitude = 36.68 (degrees)
tav = 20.34 (oC)
amp = 1.72 (oC)

year day radn maxt mint rain wind vp rh
() () (MJ/m2) (oC) (oC) (mm) (m/s) (hPa) (%)
2015 1 19.42 27.43 17.89 0.00 2.3 18.4 71
2015 2 20.11 28.12 18.03 0.00 1.9 17.9 68
...

Write an APSIM Next Generation file

For APSIM Next Generation, use format = "apsimng". This writes two files: arusha_2015.csv (data) and arusha_2015_constants.txt (site metadata).

ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2015-01-01",
  end_date   = "2015-12-31",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha_2015",
  format     = "apsimng"
)

Extract only required variables 

ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2015-01-01",
  end_date   = "2015-12-31",
  variables  = "required",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha_2015_min",
  format     = "classic"
)

Extract a custom subset of variables 

ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2015-01-01",
  end_date   = "2015-12-31",
  variables  = c("maxt", "mint", "rain", "radn", "wind"),
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha_2015_wind",
  format     = "classic"
)

Download missing files automatically

If AgERA5 files for the requested period are not yet on disk, set download = TRUE. The function will fetch any missing files before extracting, using the location derived from coords as the bounding box.

ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2015-01-01",
  end_date   = "2015-12-31",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha_2015",
  download   = TRUE
)

Relative humidity time-of-day

rh is extracted at a specific time of day. The default is "09h". Use rh_time to change this.

ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2015-01-01",
  end_date   = "2015-12-31",
  variables  = c("maxt", "mint", "rain", "radn", "rh"),
  rh_time    = "12h",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha_2015_rh12"
)

Multi-year records

To build a multi-year .met file, extend the date range. ag5_apsim() handles leap years correctly via R’s seq.Date().

ag5_apsim(
  coords     = c(36.68, -3.37),
  start_date = "2010-01-01",
  end_date   = "2020-12-31",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data",
  filename   = "C:/apsim/arusha_2010_2020",
  format     = "classic"
)
